Stage 1 admits five Jazz Gallery performances for event-specific reasons: Dabin Ryu turns a residency commission about discomfort into her first live recording; Jonathan Paik's residency commission binds hymns, sanjo, footwork, blues, free jazz, musique concrete and algorithms; Jonathan Suazo's Ricano language joins Puerto Rican and Dominican identity to Afro-Caribbean modern jazz; Capatosta removes bass and piano to foreground elastic three-way improvisation; and Alexis Cuadrado gives a five-year silent-film and social-justice project its album-release performance with a ten-piece ensemble. events.subtitle: Discomfort — album release concert
events.category: Residency-commission album release / contemporary large-ensemble jazz
events.factual_description: The Jazz Gallery presents Dabin Ryu's Discomfort album-release concert on October 31, 2026, with sets at 7:00 PM and 9:00 PM. The seven-piece ensemble features Ryu on piano with Brandon Choi, Nathan Reising, Kevin Sun, Joe Giordano, Benjamin Young and Willis Edmundson. The venue describes Discomfort as Ryu's third album, her first live recording and the outgrowth of her 2025 Jazz Gallery Residency Commission, built by deliberately moving beyond familiar compositional techniques to examine vulnerability and change.

en.why_it_matters: Ryu is not merely launching a record: she is exposing the result of a residency in which discomfort became a compositional method. The enlarged horn palette lets the music test vulnerability and instability in public, turning a personal constraint into an ensemble language rather than a theme pasted onto ordinary modern jazz.
en.trip_verdict: Catch one set if Halloween already puts New York within reach; the commission-to-live-recording arc makes the night useful to know about. From the DMV, pair it with another strong city reason instead of making a dedicated trip for this alone.

es.why_it_matters: Ryu no sólo presenta un disco: expone el resultado de una residencia donde la incomodidad se volvió método de composición. La paleta ampliada de metales y saxos deja que la música pruebe vulnerabilidad e inestabilidad en público, convirtiendo una restricción personal en lenguaje de ensamble y no en tema pegado a un jazz moderno convencional.
es.trip_verdict: Iría a uno de los sets si Halloween ya vuelve viable Nueva York; el arco entre comisión de residencia y primera grabación en vivo hace que la fecha valga tenerla presente. Desde el DMV, la combinaría con otra razón fuerte para estar en la ciudad en vez de viajar únicamente por este concierto.

events.subtitle: Catch Me Weeping in Reverent Awe — 2026 Residency Commission
events.category: Residency commission / Korean American experimental jazz and electronics
events.factual_description: The Jazz Gallery presents Jonathan Paik's 2026 Residency Commission, Catch Me Weeping in Reverent Awe, on November 6-7, 2026, with 7:00 PM and 9:00 PM sets each night. Paik leads a six-person ensemble of piano, samplers, two guitars, bass and drums. The venue describes the new compositions as drawing on hymns, Korean sanjo, footwork, blues, free jazz, musique concrete and internet algorithms while Paik connects Korean American heritage to Black American piano lineage.

Stage 1 admission rests on a newly commissioned language that explicitly places Korean sanjo and heritage beside Black American piano lineage, club-derived rhythm, free improvisation, sampling and algorithms. en.why_it_matters: Paik's commission treats lineage as working material: Korean sanjo and hymns collide with footwork, blues, free jazz, musique concrete and internet algorithms inside a band built around piano, samplers and two guitars. The point is not eclectic reference collecting but hearing a Korean American improviser test how inherited forms survive distortion, speed and digital mediation.
en.trip_verdict: Make room for one set if New York is workable that weekend; four performances give the itinerary flexibility. From farther down the corridor, pair the commission with a second strong date rather than overloading one night with scarcity it does not claim.

es.why_it_matters: La comisión de Paik trata el linaje como material de trabajo: sanjo coreano e himnos chocan con footwork, blues, free jazz, música concreta y algoritmos de internet dentro de una banda armada con piano, samplers y dos guitarras. No se trata de coleccionar referencias, sino de oír a un improvisador coreano-estadounidense probar cómo sobreviven las formas heredadas a la distorsión, la velocidad y la mediación digital.
es.trip_verdict: Le haría espacio a uno de los sets si Nueva York resulta viable ese fin de semana; cuatro funciones dan flexibilidad al itinerario. Desde más abajo del corredor, combinaría la comisión con una segunda fecha fuerte en vez de cargar una sola noche con una escasez que no reclama.

events.factual_description: The Jazz Gallery presents Alexis Cuadrado Group's Silent Film Scores for Social Justice album-release concert on November 20, 2026, with sets at 7:00 PM and 9:00 PM. The ten-piece ensemble pairs new scores with century-old silent films addressing immigration, women's rights, poverty, inequality and LGBTQ rights. The venue describes the project as five years in the making and notes that recent performances have raised funds for Make the Road New York, the Gender and Family Project and Planned Parenthood.

El atractivo no es simplemente cine con acompañamiento: maderas, metales, violín, vibráfono, guitarra, piano y sección rítmica convierten el archivo en un problema vivo de ensamble, mientras el historial de beneficios obliga a que el discurso social se mida con acciones.
